checkpoint_review: The Router's checkpoint verdicts are largely accurate. The 'Underside connects to a long stabilizer bar mechanism' was correctly marked as untestable due to the viewing angle. All visible geometric and material checkpoints (elongated shape, blank label, matte finish, central position) were correctly identified as present. The Router did not miss any obvious structural failures in the space bar itself.
artifact_review: The Router identified text anomalies (severity 2) and slight geometric distortion (severity 1). The Image Text Auditor confirmed the absence of legible text ('full_extracted_text': ''), which supports the Router's observation of 'soft/melted' legends—effectively, the AI failed to render crisp characters, resulting in noise or gibberish that the OCR could not pick up. This is a notable artifact for a keyboard image. The Perceptual Quality Auditor noted slight compression/graininess (score 0.2), which aligns with the Router's minor severity ratings. The Topology Auditor found a clean mask (confidence 0.9586), suggesting no major fusion or fragmentation of the space bar itself. However, the lack of legible text on the *other* keys is a significant quality defect for a realistic keyboard generation, even if the target class is just the space bar.
alignment_reasoning: The image strongly conforms to the 'space bar' class. The Fine Grained Classifier ranked 'space bar' as the top candidate with high confidence (logit 7.66). All testable diagnostic checkpoints passed. The object is clearly identifiable as a space bar on a keyboard.
artifact_reasoning: While the space bar itself is structurally sound (high topology confidence), the surrounding context exhibits AI artifacts. Specifically, the key legends are illegible/gibberish (confirmed by empty OCR output), which is a common generative failure. The Router rated this as severity 2; I maintain this as it doesn't affect the target class directly but degrades overall realism. Slight geometric warping on the right edge and minor compression noise further reduce the artifact score from perfect. It is better than the 'mid' reference (altar) which had structural confusion, but worse than the 'high' reference (rifle) which was crisp and artifact-free.
